name: Handle errors and keep the workflow going
description: Learn how an Error Handler keeps a workflow running when a step fails. The workflow calls a test URL that always fails; the Error Handler runs its error branch instead of stopping, and a final step proves the workflow kept going. It runs with one click and needs no connection.
shortDescription: Learn how an Error Handler keeps a workflow running when a step fails.
keyFeatures: Wrap steps that can fail in an Error Handler
Run a CATCH branch instead of stopping the workflow
See a failed step's error in the run panel
Continue with the rest of the workflow after a failure
idealFor: First-time ByteChef users who want their workflows to survive a failing API call.
steps: Trigger: the workflow starts when you click Test in the workflow editor.
Catch errors: an Error Handler runs its TRY branch: Call a failing API (an HTTP GET to httpbin.org/status/500) and Log the success.
The HTTP call fails, so the TRY branch stops and the CATCH branch runs: the Logger writes that the request failed.
Log that the workflow kept going: after the Error Handler, the Logger writes that the workflow continued.
